reason: Proposes an undescribed 'technique for the alignment of class distribution' (oversampling per keywords) with no detail or named parts, so the scheme cannot be told.
SMART-SMOTE is a new SMOTE variant with noise removal, feature selection and dissimilarity-based neighbours; results are only against unnamed state-of-the-art methods.

RS-DAAL puts existing under/over/hybrid resampling inside an adversarial active learning loop and compares these resampling techniques; whether the resampling chain rather than the active-learning framework is the contribution is borderline.
MNDO-NC is the authors' new oversampler (multivariate normal sampling plus kNN voting for categorical features), compared with 6 sampling methods.
Proposes FOS, a new fuzzy information decomposition oversampler used with ROS/RUS in a voting ensemble; no comparison against other resampling is stated and the generator kind is uncertain.

HardVis is a visual analytics tool in which users apply and validate existing under/oversamplers on chosen instance-hardness types; no sampler of its own, though user-steered targeting could be read as a new way of applying.
ISMOTE is a modified SMOTE that iteratively generates near misclassified samples, compared with SMOTE and other oversamplers.
SSPD is a new prototype-guided, feature-weighted SMOTE interpolation for hyperspectral data; compared only with individual classifiers.

DAFL applies a 'dynamic SMOTE' (dynamic minority oversampling, change not described) with drift test and client weighting in federated learning; read as a newly named oversampler, compared only with unnamed baselines.
DEBOHID is a new differential-evolution-based oversampler compared with nine oversampling methods.
Besides a CNN-AE/MLP ECG model, states that new oversampling and undersampling approaches are proposed (not described); compared only before against after.
Improved SMOTE using a kNN graph and GCN, followed by AE-GAN regeneration, a stated new two-stage generator; no named resampling comparison.
DCAES is a convolutional autoencoder with SMOTE (an existing sampler in a learned space) followed by DBSCAN undersampling and Tomek links, with no stated change; comparison partners not named.
Triangle SMOTE is an improved SMOTE interpolating within three-point triangles, followed by an IPF filter; no comparison with other resampling stated.

GAVAE is described only as combining a VAE with GAN adversarial training (a standard VAE-GAN hybrid) with no further stated change; could be read as a new architecture, compared with unnamed traditional methods.
Boundary-prioritized FCM-SMOTE is a new SMOTE variant weighting interpolation by fuzzy membership; compared only unsampled vs sampled and with state-of-the-art IDS.
WOOLASVM is a new weighted online oversampling scheme that dynamically oversamples the SVM boundary in streams; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
nDeepSMOTEc is DeepSMOTE modified for tabular data (a stated change), compared with other oversampling techniques.
DBE splits data into lower-ratio subsets and applies a modified ASUWO oversampler in a new balancing ensemble; compared only with other ensemble models.
Fed-DiTTab employs a tabular diffusion transformer (DiTTab) per client in federated learning; the abstract does not say whether DiTTab is new or a standard diffusion model used as is.
GDO is a new oversampler with probabilistic anchor selection and Gaussian generation; compared with 'imbalanced learning approaches' not said to be resampling.
Pretrained diffusion model with standard LoRA fine-tuning on the rare class, used as is for augmentation at varied ratios; compared only with real data alone.
ICOS (Improved Correlation over Sampling) is a newly named oversampler whose mechanism is not described; no comparison stated.
OHCM is named as a hybrid of oversampling, CutMix and Mixup, standard augmentation parts with no stated change, inside the EMBL long-tailed model; compared only with state-of-the-art accuracy.
DCIA is a new multiclass prototype generation method that inserts and search-adjusts class prototypes; compared only with ensemble classifiers.
NaNG-SMOTE is a new SMOTE variant using a natural neighbourhood graph, noise removal and weighted subgraph-core interpolation, compared with 8 oversamplers.

A weight decision algorithm sets how many samples to create per minority example from edge-detection gradients, a new allocation; general oversampling is named only as the aim, with no comparison reported.

ILMNN is a new imbalance-aware metric learning (with reweighting and KL safeguard) that makes a space for unnamed existing oversamplers; read as an existing sampler in a learned space, though the space is the paper's own; comparators unnamed.
SB-SVM-ensemble chains standard SMOTE with Bagging and SVM, presented as the new method and compared with SMOTE-SVM and a partition-based SVM ensemble.
Searched augmentation policies enlarge the minority set, then a standard PGGAN generates minority SAR images with no stated change; evaluated only before against after.
Proposes 'liner to pattern-sampling', a new regression/correlation-based way to create samples, compared with SMOTE and classifiers; the abstract is unclear on the generation mechanism.
NC_Link_MWMOTE replaces the clustering in MWMOTE with NC_Link hierarchical clustering, a stated change; compared with an unnamed baseline.
FDFRL includes a kernel-guided adversarial generator with hierarchical adversarial refinement, read as a new generative module, within federated RL fraud detection; compared with unnamed baselines.
KTS is a new K-means triangular synthesis oversampler generating by cluster density, paired with a pinball-loss LDM; comparators not named.
RAMGANH combines range-based association-rule undersampling with a modified TGAN (a stated change); compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
cCGen is a new conditional classifier-generator augmentation algorithm, compared with SMOTE, ADASYN and cWGAN-GP.
Existing synthetic oversamplers (SMOTE/ADASYN per keywords) applied in a fused image-metadata embedding space, presented as the key contribution; compared only with image-only baselines.
HSMOTE is a new SMOTE-inspired module that synthesises hypergraph vertices and their high-order correlations, within the HGHC framework; compared only with state-of-the-art.
Two new density-based sampling algorithms (undersampling, and under- plus unnamed oversampling) compared with other balancing algorithms.
Generates pseudo-fault samples by its own wavelet phase-space reconstruction of signal energy regions, a generator of the paper's own; no resampling comparison; generator kind uncertain.
GraphAdasyn extends adaptive synthetic sampling to multiclass imbalanced node classification on graphs, a stated change; compared with unnamed baselines.
New LLM-based oversampler with label-and-feature conditioning, a new permutation fine-tuning strategy and training on interpolated samples (stated changes); compared with unnamed SOTA baselines.

CorrOV-CSEn uses correlation-based oversampling with a customised rate and zone (a new way of applying SMOTE) inside a cost-sensitive AdaBoost; the abstract hints this oversampler may come from earlier work.
Uses advanced elk herd optimisation to search SMOTE sampling rates, a search for how much to oversample, before a BiLSTM IDS; no resampling comparison.
NCLO-SMOTE is a new algorithm with semi-supervised clustering, Newton-cooling overlap cleaning and cluster-weighted oversampling, compared with ten sampling methods.

NB-MIO changes SMOTE's base-instance choice to safe minority samples found by a second Tomek-link search after Tomek cleaning, a stated change rather than a plain SMOTE+Tomek chain; 15 comparators not said to be resampling.

An LLM-routing paper that also proposes text augmentation plus a perplexity-based dynamic weighted/oversampling allocation; read as a new allocation, but the parts may be standard and resampling is secondary.
SSMOTE, a newly named stable SMOTE whose change is not described, is compared with other data augmentation methods for chiller fault data.
New rough-set undersampling plus multi-objective evolutionary oversampling guided by KL divergence and attribute dependency, compared with existing resampling techniques.
GMM-SMOTE is an improved oversampler that clusters with GMM, allocates by cluster density and screens by KL distance; no resampling comparison stated.
SHAP feature selection, t-SNE latent mapping and Gaussian noise sampling of minority points, all standard parts with no stated change; no resampling comparison.

Improved SMOTE that checks class crossing from the minority distribution, generates across classes when crossing is severe and reweights non-borderline positives; compared with unnamed 'other methods'.
LoRAS is a new localized random affine shadowsampling oversampler, compared with SMOTE and several SMOTE extensions.
Develops a multi-kernel over-sampling (MKOS) that generates in the kernel space learned by its own MKMFA, a newly named oversampler with the mechanism not detailed; comparators unnamed.

OHSEC uses density-peak-guided under/oversampling with validation-based optimisation of task-specific imbalance ratios (a search for how much to resample) and evidence fusion; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
TDGN introduces a density-based WGAN (a stated modification) to reduce behavioural overlap, with a time-aware gated network; compared with unnamed competitors.
DRCW-ASEG is a new multiclass OVO algorithm that dynamically generates minority examples during competence weighting; no resampling comparison stated.

Proposes a multi-kernel over-sampling within a multi-kernel feature selection framework for nodule false-positive reduction, a newly named oversampler not described; compared with unnamed competing methods.
Oversamples with SMOTE, clusters the synthetic samples by GMM and keeps them by majority-based cluster weights (a new allocation per region), compared with SMOTE and variants.
IMSMOTE is an improved SMOTE adding randomness and probability to synthesis, used in a GRC-SVM credit risk framework; compared with unnamed existing approaches.
New multiclass oversampling technique based on intra- and inter-class distance matrices, compared with common oversampling techniques.
New hypersphere-based over/undersampling driven by boosting sample weights and learning difficulty inside a reweighted AdaBoost; no resampling comparison stated.
SDD-SMOTE is an improved SMOTE that oversamples according to a designed sample distribution density model; no comparison stated.

Standard GAN oversampling followed by a novel adaptive neighbourhood-weighted undersampler of the paper's own that removes generated and majority instances; the generator is unchanged, so this may be read as generator plus filter.
FC-SMOTE is named as fuzzy clustering plus SMOTE with no change described (a new name over standard parts), and is compared with traditional oversampling algorithms.
A deep neural network is used to oversample EEG movement data, but the abstract gives no detail of the model, so own versus standard cannot be told; evaluated before against after.
A sliding-window SMOTE is developed to preserve temporal dependencies (a changed SMOTE), alongside feature selection and BiLSTM-GRU; compared only with classifier models.
VAHMSE adds mutual information to the VAE loss to prevent posterior collapse (a stated change) for anomaly data generation; compared with state-of-the-art models only.
Improved Random-SMOTE that uses SVM support vectors as parent samples, a stated change; no comparison stated.
TDCGAN is a new triple-discriminator conditional GAN architecture, compared with SMOTE and RandomOverSampler.
Graph oversampling with SMOTE on node representations plus an edge generator trained with a new abnormal-connectivity margin loss (a stated change to the generator); no resampling comparison.
TDDMRT proposes a KNN-Jaccard minority resampling method with an enhanced drift detector for streams, compared with existing over- and undersampling techniques.
New oversampler generating minority samples by genetic crossover within K-means clusters; evaluated only with KNN and SVM.
Proposes an enhanced SMOTE guided by clustering and PCA, PPO-chosen augmentation and DQN-based sampling; no comparison with other resampling stated.

Samples tail-class features from calibrated distributions borrowed from few-shot distribution calibration, applied as is in feature space; could be read as own calibrated sampling; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art.
DG-SMOTE is a new genetic-programming oversampler that evolves how selected instances are combined, with a distance-angle fitness, compared with popular sampling methods.
M2M-VAEGAN adds VGM feature handling, majority pre-training with balanced fine-tuning and an auxiliary classifier to a VAE-GAN (stated changes), compared with SMOTE, CTGAN and CTABGAN.
A 1-D DCGAN, a standard architecture adapted to range profiles with no other stated change, generates HRRPs; compared with state-of-the-art oversampling methods.
GNUS is called novel but its name describes only standard Gaussian-noise upsampling with no change stated; compared with seven conventional correction methods including random oversampling.
M-D2GAN modifies the GAN with type-specific generation of mixed variables and an added normal-class discriminator, compared with the classic GAN.
MGS-GRF is a new mixed-feature oversampler using KDE with locally estimated full-rank covariances plus generalized random forest for categorical features, compared with SMOTE-NC and other strategies.

GraphBalance does SMOTE in a learned node-embedding space with a jointly trained edge generator; the abstract appears to be the GraphSMOTE abstract under a new name, so coded as an existing method; compared with unnamed baselines.
ISMOTE (2011) randomises interpolation within the ball formed by a minority instance and its neighbour, compared with SMOTE.
Extends SAM-kNN with SMOTE and kENN for drifting streams and proposes a new Informed Downsampling method shown superior to these balancing variants.
Devises a PSO-based metaheuristic data balancer (mechanism not described) with GA classifier tuning, compared with random undersampling.
Surrounding-neighbourhood SMOTE variants (Gabriel graph, relative neighbourhood graph, nearest centroid) change SMOTE's neighbour choice, compared with other oversamplers.
Improved clustering SMOTE with KNN noise removal, density-based sub-cluster weights and interpolation toward sub-cluster centres (a new allocation and interpolation); comparators not named.

A cGAN with standard spectral normalisation and self-attention, followed by a quality gate (discriminator score, SSIM, FID) and sample weighting; read as a standard generator plus filter; evaluated before against after.
Enhanced SMOTE incorporating feature correlations into synthesis, compared with traditional SMOTE and no SMOTE.
A hybrid ensemble combining existing undersampling and oversampling with Bagging/AdaBoost, no stated change, within a comparative study of resampling methods.
MOT2LD is a new oversampler weighting minority samples by local densities in a low-dimensional clustered space, compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN and MWMOTE.
Autoencoder dimensionality reduction plus K-means-supported oversampling, a chain of standard parts with no stated change; evaluated without resampling comparison.
BHTF introduces a novel Proximity-Driven Undersampling combined with SMOTE in a multi-label Hoeffding tree forest; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
CTD/CTDE select key minority samples for SMOTE by a cost-aware three-way decision over CCA covers, a new way of applying SMOTE; comparators unnamed.
VMSG generates samples from 'volunteer' minority instances chosen by an OC-SVM with a new BaM loss, compared with SMOTE variants, GANs and VAEs.
KNNOR is a new three-step KNN oversampler using compactness and relative density, compared with ten oversamplers.
DCI-ISSA-RF proposes Data Center Interpolation oversampling with sparrow-search RF tuning; compared with unnamed famous approaches.
GBO and SSG are named only as GAN oversampling and SVM-SMOTE chained with a GAN, standard parts with no stated change to the GAN; compared with SMOTE.
AR-GAN adds an activation reconstruction loss to image-translation GAN (a new loss), compared with classical data augmentation.
Proposes a hybrid probabilistic oversampling (newly named, not described) alongside sparse group lasso features; compared with unnamed baseline and state-of-the-art.
CASS is a new adaptive oversampler using GMM subcluster centres, proximity-density weights and tailored synthesis, compared with nine sampling algorithms.
R-SMOTE synthesises from reverse nearest neighbours of a selected minority set, a new SMOTE variant compared with four standard oversamplers.

A 3D conditional latent diffusion model conditioned on tumour mask and IDH status with two added attention modules in the UNet, read as a new architecture and conditioning; no comparison with other augmentation.
MPMU is a new algorithm that clusters by imbalance degree, penalises majority instances per cluster and upsamples the minority; no resampling comparison.
Dual-tier oversampling chains GPT-2 text generation, used as is, with SMOTE; compared only with existing models.
WOASD removes noise, sets per-sample synthesis counts from distance and density weights and synthesises with an improved SMOTE; compared with unnamed traditional methods.
Entropy-based ambiguity zones guide targeted oversampling, a new allocation of synthetic examples by region, compared with global SMOTE.
Radius-SMOTE generates within a safe radius after initial selection, a new SMOTE variant; comparators not named.
WIMOTE is a newly named within-class oversampler with a 'statistical oversample strategy' and noise removal, compared with SMOTE.
Uses an adaptive subspace self-organising map, with its own local mapping and competitive rule, to generate minority samples, compared with existing oversamplers.
GAN with a restructured Transformer-ECA generator and a dual-function classifying discriminator (new architecture); compared with unnamed state-of-the-art algorithms.
The diagnosis scheme contains a novel imputation-based oversampling technique whose mechanism is not described; no resampling comparison.
Applies the authors' earlier RN-SMOTE (SMOTE plus DBSCAN noise removal) to multiclass data with no change described, compared with traditional SMOTE.
Designs an oversampling approach with optimised deep clustering, inheritance theory and Mahalanobis distance for Argo error samples, within a siamese ConvLSTM; no resampling comparison.
WCB-OT is a new optimal-transport generator using Wasserstein barycentres and morphology costs, compared with StyleGAN2 and SMOTE.
NPONN is a new parameter-free natural-neighbour oversampler with noise filtering and adaptive neighbour counts; no comparison named.
Generates minority fraud records by one-point genetic crossover, an oversampler of the paper's own; only classifiers are compared.
Improved GraphSMOTE with k-hop topological constraints (a stated change) inside a temporal heterogeneous graph fraud model; compared with GNN baselines.
MC-MBRC is a new multiclass membership-based resampling with noise removal, interpolation oversampling and energy-based cleaning; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art.
OIRP optimises how many samples to generate and where, a search for how much to oversample applied to existing oversamplers, compared with classical and SOTA oversamplers.
A new outlier generation method reflecting body-weight volatility and periodicity, compared with SMOTE-based and GAN-based augmentation.

Introduces a modified CutMix augmentation for class imbalance (stated as modified, not described) within an attention HRNet for building localisation and damage classification; compared with state-of-the-art models.
A conditional WGAN-GP with a CBAM attention mechanism added to the generator, a stated architecture change; evaluated only across classifiers.
CCG-taming transformers improves the generator's encoder with SE and MultiRes blocks and layer normalisation (stated changes), with SMOTE-Tomek and T2T-ViT; no resampling comparison.
CAHS is a new chemistry-informed oversampler recombining BRICS fragments, with confidence-weighted loss; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art.
Clusters the minority with K-means, then an improved SMOTE handles continuous and discrete features separately (a stated change), before an ensemble; no resampling comparison named.
RSP-CCFD introduces SAE-SMOTE, a newly named interpolation oversampler meant to reduce overlap (mechanism not described), compared with eight data-level and algorithm-level methods.
BFGAN is a modified GAN with an added boundary-importance label and multimodality-aware structure for time series; comparators not named.
wLOF-ADASYN fuses modified LOF weights with ADASYN weights and constrains generation, a new variant compared with traditional oversamplers.

Minority attribute augmentation mixes two images and oversamples minority attribute classes (mixup-style parts with no stated change) inside a compositional zero-shot transformer; compared only on overall SoTA.

Partitions the input space by MST-based clustering into local linear partitions and applies an unnamed existing oversampler within each, like clustering then SMOTE; the boundary-aligned partitioning could be read as a new way of applying; no comparison stated.
SPWGAN adds FFT physics constraints to the adversarial training (physics-constrained generation) with spectral normalisation; no comparison with other generators stated.
SEDA is a new similarity- and feature-importance-based minority augmentation, compared with random oversampling and SMOTE.

CFA-SMOTE combines an existing instance-based counterfactual method with standard SMOTE, no change described, compared with counterfactual and class-imbalance methods; target is grass growth with outlier events treated as a minority class.
RSMOTE divides the minority into four density regions and resamples per region, a new SMOTE variant; compared only across its own region variants.
Hybrid of standard SMOTE and additive white Gaussian noise augmentation with no stated change, compared with each technique alone and undersampling; the chain contains a standard augmentation.
New entropy-maximising distance-based resampling that undersamples dense and oversamples sparse areas; comparators not named.
SW uses complete random forest space division and weights to filter noise and set the position of new samples for existing oversamplers, compared against those oversamplers.
Develops a DTW-distance variant of SMOTE for heartbeats alongside a focal-modulation network; no resampling comparison.
Introduces quantum oversampling, selecting instances with a quantum operator, as an original component with PSO-tuned imputation and feature selection; compared with unnamed algorithms.
Proposes decision-tree-based undersampling and an adaptive subregional SMOTE weighted by overlap density; compared with benchmark models.
NNW-CCRS is a new neighbourhood-weighted convex-combination oversampler; compared only with no data expansion.
BCONDS is a new oversampler generating counterfactuals from majority neighbours of borderline minority instances after isolation-forest noise removal; comparators unnamed.
MAHAKIL is a new inheritance-based oversampler, compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN and ROS.
TFDL-GAN adds FFT-based time-frequency dual loss to GAN training (a new loss), compared with GAN, VAE and SMOTE.
DST-GAN adds a differentiable Dempster-Shafer fusion component for multimodal oversampling (new architecture); compared with unnamed strong baselines.
ADAIN-SMOTE evolves an adaptive artificial immune network with new operators to augment the minority before SMOTE, compared with 8 oversamplers.
OS-CCD sets how many SMOTE samples each positive gets from a classification contribution degree, a new allocation, compared with six oversamplers.
Kernel-based oversampling generates in SVM feature space and maps back via pre-images, compared with an existing oversampling technique.
KTE-SMOTE chains silhouette-tuned k-means SMOTE, Tomek links and ENN but also smooths the boundary during generation (a stated change), compared with traditional SMOTE.

An improved SMOTE using a mutual-information dropout sparse autoencoder space, natural-neighbour noise removal and different oversampling for borderline and centre samples; compared only with measured data.
LATE-SMOTE is described only as SMOTE operating in the autoencoder's latent space (a new name over an existing sampler in a learned space); compared with FixMatch, not with resampling.

CoDSA fine-tunes standard pretrained generators but conditions synthesis on under-sampled regions with a theory of synthetic volume and region allocation, read as new conditioning/allocation; compared with non-adaptive augmentation.
CFCPred uses its own cluster-purity-guided resampling that synthesises from sample, neighbour and cluster relations, with fuzzy voting; no resampling comparison.

MIAC applies ADASYN only to samples on which a mutual-information classifier abstains, read as a new choice of where to oversample; it could also be read as a chain of existing parts; compared only with MIC.

CADA is a newly named cluster-based adaptive augmentation whose adaptive mechanism is not described, distinct from the cluster-based oversampling and random augmentation it is compared with alongside ROS and SMOTE.
Theoretical analysis of SMOTE leads to two new SMOTE variants, compared with SMOTE and 10 rebalancing methods including deep generative ones.
MalImgDA fine-tunes a pretrained diffusion model on few-shot malware images with no stated change; compared with unnamed commonly used approaches.
New margin-enhanced synthesis with label-propagation pruning of majority outliers and a K+1-class discriminator; compared with unnamed baselines.
New optimal-transport oversampler with a novel regularisation shifting the minority distribution; no named comparison.
BED is a new density-based resampling that removes noisy majority examples and generates minority examples, compared with SMOTE.
KHOI-SMOTE interpolates toward across-cluster sparse areas chosen by an h-outlyingness index, compared with SMOTE and its variants.
Proposes two improved SMOTE algorithms limiting the generation range, before a stacked LSTM; compared only with classifiers.
ICD-Balancer is a cGAN-based improved SMOTE approach with a proposed Gumbel-Sigmoid for mixed tabular features (a stated change), for ICU survival analysis; comparators not named.
CDAF adds a contrastive alignment loss, class-conditioned latent space and staged training to a generator (new loss and training); no named comparison.
HCAB-SMOTE removes majority noise and oversamples selected k-means clusters of the borderline, compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, AB-SMOTE and CAB-SMOTE.
RBO is a new radial-basis-function guided oversampler, compared with state-of-the-art imbalanced data preprocessing methods.
Applies standard Markov-chain and LSTM text generation, used as is, to create minority texts, compared with traditional oversampling.
Proposes layer oversampling and its hybrid with error-bootstrap oversampling for ramp events, compared with other sampling methods.
An improved DCGAN (stated as improved) generates fault samples after wavelet multi-sensor fusion; no resampling comparison.
AWGSENN weights minority instances adaptively and generates with a designed Gaussian density before ENN cleaning, compared with five oversampling and two hybrid methods.
An improved CycleGAN with added spectral normalisation and weight decay (stated changes) generates fault time-frequency maps; compared only with classifiers.
New extrapolated Markov chain text oversampler estimating transitions partly from the majority, compared with prominent oversamplers.
Two-cluster segmentation then standard SMOTE and ADASYN within each cluster, presented as the method and compared with standard resampling.
Proposes an improved SMOTE (change not described) with repeated sampling and a Choquet fuzzy integral ensemble; compared only with ensemble techniques.
DSMOTE is a new oversampler using diversity and separability measures to remove abnormal samples and select seeds, evaluated against four resampling algorithms.

SynKGen is described as Gaussian perturbations, scaled by variance, applied in a kernel PCA space (a new name over a standard noise sampler in a learned space); the variance control could be read as own; compared with ADASYN and SMOTE.

SHAP-selected critical and near-boundary samples steer a classifier-guided conditional diffusion model with a Transformer denoiser, read as a new allocation and conditioning; compared with SMOTE/ADASYN and CGAN/TimeGAN.
SMOTE-IDEA is an optimised SMOTE with feature selection, sample filtering and density-weighted generation, compared with traditional SMOTE.

G-TOD applies distribution calibration with generative oversampling of the rare class on aligned features (an existing calibrated sampler in a learned space), within a cross-domain graph fraud framework; no resampling comparison.

GEP-NB is a classifier using 'a simple mechanism' to generate minority examples and gene-specific selection of them; the abstract does not say whether these are standard or new; compared only with classifiers.
An off-the-shelf LLM generates synthetic sensor samples via standard prompting strategies, used as is; compared with SMOTE and random sampling.
Modifies SMOTE (weighted SMOTE, change not described) with an expert-judgement voting ensemble; compared only with traditional models.
IADASYN improves ADASYN with LOF outlier removal and special handling of categorical features, compared with classifiers built on classical sampling methods.
SSMOTE adds support and roulette-wheel selection and heterogeneous neighbour information to SMOTE; compared with 'algorithms in pertinent literatures' not said to be resampling.

KNN typing and clustering-based undersampling of the majority plus a tabular WGAN-GP (no stated change) for the minority, standard parts combined; the undersampling scheme could be read as own; no resampling comparison.
GOIO combines a triplet-centre-loss VAE with a class-centre-prompted conditional latent diffusion model (new loss and conditioning), compared with state-of-the-art oversamplers.
Proposes JSO, a dynamic neighbour selection oversampler based on JS divergence, within a transfer-learning SVM tuned by a new ivy optimiser; no resampling comparison.
MKC-SMOTE is a new multiclass SMOTE scheme with class-aware seed selection, enhanced interpolation and undersampling post-processing, compared with oversampling methods.

WECOI balances stream chunks with 'our hybrid approach' of over-sampling and instance selection inside a weighted one-class ensemble, but the abstract does not say whether these techniques are new or standard; no comparison stated.
AR-ADASYN is a new adaptive oversampler using angle and radius between minority samples, compared with other oversamplers.
DENI is a new hybrid sampling framework with density-gap noise detection and density-enhanced neighbourhood oversampling; no named comparison.
Proposes stable SMOTE-based variants that remove randomness in seed, neighbour and interpolation steps, compared with the SMOTE-based techniques.
FID is a new fuzzy information decomposition method that creates minority samples while estimating missing values; compared with individual and combination methods not said to be resampling.

GO-SMOTE replaces SMOTE interpolation with sampling from a fitted GMM then ENN cleaning, i.e. standard GMM sampling and an existing cleaner under a SMOTE name; could be read as a changed SMOTE; compared with unnamed similar technologies.
Mostly a status review that 'proposed an algorithm based on de-noising oversampling technology' with no detail, so whether the oversampler is new cannot be told.
